fields.subject: SQL Server Type Mapping
fields.trigger: IsValidType evaluates a candidate CLR property type
fields.response: return true only for exactly the CLR shapes declared for that variant: the string-family variants (NVarChar, NChar, VarChar, Char) accept a plain string, any enum type, or a Nullable<T> whose underlying type is an enum (there is no plain nullable-string form); MapToSqlBigIntAttribute accepts long, any enum type, or Nullable<long> only — a Nullable<T> whose underlying type is an enum is NOT accepted; MapToSqlIntAttribute, MapToSqlSmallIntAttribute, and MapToSqlTinyIntAttribute each accept their declared integer primitive (int, short, or byte respectively), any enum type, a Nullable<T> of that primitive, or a Nullable<T> whose underlying type is an enum; the single-primitive scalar variants accept only their declared CLR type or the Nullable<T> form of that type, with no enum acceptance — Bit: bool; Decimal, Money, SmallMoney: decimal; Float: double; Real: float; DateTime, DateTime2: DateTime; Date: DateOnly; DateTimeOffset: DateTimeOffset; UniqueIdentifier: Guid; MapToSqlTimeAttribute accepts TimeSpan, TimeOnly, Nullable<TimeSpan>, or Nullable<TimeOnly>, with no enum acceptance; MapToSqlVarBinaryAttribute and MapToSqlBinaryAttribute each accept only byte[], with no Nullable<T> wrapper, no enum acceptance, and no span or memory alternative — ReadOnlySpan<byte>, Span<byte>, ReadOnlyMemory<byte> and Memory<byte> are rejected; MapToSqlJsonAttribute accepts only System.Text.Json.JsonDocument, with no Nullable<T> wrapper and no enum acceptance
fields.postcondition: the mapping builder can distinguish supported from unsupported property types; a candidate type outside the stated set for that variant returns false, so a model property of that type is rejected with InvalidMapTypeException when its mapping is first built, and every accepted type works through input parameters, output parameters, data-reader reads and table-valued-parameter rows
